# Capturefab

> Capturefab is a camera capture CLI for macOS, Windows and Linux. Use it to find cameras, read or change settings, save images and record video.

Capturefab supports GigE Vision and USB3 Vision cameras with GenICam controls. It also opens webcams, network streams and video files. Release binaries include FFmpeg for media input and recording. Use `sim:0` for capture and control examples without camera hardware.

## For agents

- [Agent instructions](agents.md) cover the JSON contract, command permissions, workflows and error recovery.
- [Command reference](reference.html) lists commands, flags, JSON fields and errors.
- Run `capturefab schema` for the installed version's command list. Run `capturefab schema COMMAND` for one command, including subcommands such as `jobs wait`.

## Contract in brief

- Pass `--json` or set `CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1`. Most commands write one JSON line to stdout. Success gives a result and failure gives an `error` object with `code`, `message` and optional `hint` and `details`.
- `watch` and `shell` write one JSON line per measurement or command. `capture -o -` writes the image to stdout and its JSON document to stderr. `--help` and `--version` print text.
- Use exit codes for the category and `error.code` for the reason. Exit codes are 0 for success, 1 for failure, 2 for invalid input, 3 for unavailable resources, 4 for timeout, 5 for unsupported operations and 6 for full storage. Interruptions use 130 (SIGINT), 143 (SIGTERM) or 129 (SIGHUP).
- Pass a camera ID from `list` with `-c`. The selector also accepts a serial, IP address, RTSP, SRT, HTTP(S) or ONVIF URL, file path or simulator. Quote selectors and feature names with shell characters.
- To receive an externally controlled GigE multicast stream, use the quoted `gige-monitor://CAMERA_IP?interface=HOST_IP&mac=12_HEX_DIGITS` selector. It performs read-only setup and passive image receiving, with no camera settings or acquisition commands; see the camera guide for channel, interface and source-port requirements. Omit settings, auto and positive device settling or capture freshness options.
- Use duration units, such as `250ms`, `2s` or `1h30m`. Use `{seq}` in capture and recording filenames to keep existing outputs.
- The automatic session keeps a camera open for 60 seconds by default. Use `--keep 5m` to extend that time or `--no-session` for one command.
- With `--background`, read the returned `job.id`. Use `jobs wait --json ID` to follow it. Use `jobs stop --json ID` to stop it and keep files already saved.

## Common calls

- Find cameras: `capturefab list --json`. Add `--kind sim` to find the default simulator.
- See supported controls: `capturefab info --json -c sim:0`.
- Measure exposure and focus: `capturefab inspect --json -c sim:0 --preview none`.
- Change exposure and measure again: `capturefab inspect --json -c sim:0 --set exposure=5ms --preview none`.
- Save a PNG: `capturefab capture --json -c sim:0 -o 'shots/{seq}.png'`.
- Measure the saved frame and log its provenance: `capturefab capture --json -c sim:0 -o shot.png --inspect --manifest shots.jsonl`.
- Start a time lapse: `capturefab capture --json -c sim:0 --every 1s --for 5s -o 'lapse/{seq}.png' --background`.
- Record video: `capturefab record --json -c sim:0 -o clip.mp4 --for 2s`.
- Stream measurements to stdout: `capturefab watch --json -c sim:0 --for 2s`.
- Record industrial signals: `capturefab data record --config sources.json --for 30s -o run.jsonl`. Get configuration examples and adapter requirements from `capturefab data protocols --json`.
- Assign a temporary GigE camera address only when requested: `capturefab network force-ip --help`. The camera must be closed; the MAC, interface and IPv4 tuple are explicit. Check post-send uncertainty before repeating.
- Trigger configured GigE action sinks: retain and arm the camera first, configure its write-only key via `set --write-only` in an explicit existing named session, then use local `network action` with explicit mode/interface/keys/mask. Optional --action-time-ticks requests an absolute device timestamp, without clock qualification; zero/past may act immediately and post-send failures may leave a future action queued. ACK success and sent-only success do not prove execution or frame arrival; wait for the capture job separately. No PTP synchronization is inferred.
- Export industrial signals: `capturefab data export run.jsonl -o run.csv` or `--format jsonl`.
- Diagnose setup: `capturefab doctor --json`.

Standard BiColor: unpacked RGBG/BGRG 8/10/12 convert to color with bounded horizontal interpolation; RAW preserves normalized native components, and FFV1 retains wide reconstructed RGB.

Industrial data: passive Micro-Epsilon ILD2300 single-DIST1 RS422 raw codes, native camera stills, Keyence KV Host Link, LS ELECTRIC XGT/XGB FEnet, Yokogawa FA-M3 PC Link, Modbus TCP with gateway unit selection and optional TLS, Modbus RTU and ASCII, classic S7 absolute and indexed reads, SLC/MicroLogix PCCC files including whole timer/counter and ST string elements over EtherNet/IP or serial DF1, SLC 5/05 files including whole timer/counter and ST string elements over legacy CSPv4, PLC-5/E files over EtherNet/IP, Beckhoff ADS, Mitsubishi SLMP 3E binary or ASCII including step/retentive devices and whole four-word iQ-R long-timer records, MC 1E and serial FX Computer Link, Panasonic FP MEWTOCOL-COM, and Omron FINS TCP/UDP, serial Host Link (including explicit legacy CPM/SRM1 native areas) and CompoWay/F reads, BACnet/IP meter and controller values, IEC 62056-21 and passive SML optical meter readouts, shared-bus SDI-12 environmental sensors through a USB serial bridge, Vaisala WXT530 serial weather measurements, HART process measurements through a managed Microflex modem, SICK TiM/LMS single scans over configured CoLa A/B, passive SICK multiScan100/picoScan100 Compact scan/IMU datagrams and explicit picoScan150 encoder/mixed UDP streams, LRS4000 Compact TCP scans and multiScan200 Compact TCP scans, ambient light and IMU, passive NMEA GNSS GGA/RMC positions, passive Velodyne VLP-16/HDL-32E raw UDP groups, passive Gocator GDP profile and surface archives, TCP/serial JSONL sensors (Unix terminals or Windows COM ports), and SCPI instruments over raw TCP, native serial, VXI-11, HiSLIP or USBTMC (`usb` feature), METTLER TOLEDO MT-SICS weights over TCP or serial, A&D standard-format Q measurements over configured serial or transparent TCP bridges, Sartorius SBI16/22 manual-print measurements over configured no-flow interfaces, MQTT/TCP or verified TLS (QoS 0–2) and EtherNet/IP reads of Logix atomic tags, explicit DWORD/packed BOOL reads and STRING members, Micro800 numeric and counted STRING values and Omron NJ/NX variables and CIP Assembly data, plus ifm IO-Link process input and the standard IO-Link JSON GET interface; passive EtherCAT, Profinet RT, CAN and CAN FD on Linux; built-in OPC-UA Read and explicit queued subscription client with optional pinned SignAndEncrypt, native quality/IEEE/timestamp fields and bounded Republish recovery. Subscription ACKs confirm local receipt with a crash gap before JSONL persistence. Explicit helpers also support Windows 10/Server 2016+ absolute .exe paths with creation-time job containment. Native Keyence IV inspection results, Cognex In-Sight cell reads and complete Cognex DataMan ID Reader result attributes can share a recording. DataMan retains raw bytes/codes without triggering or acknowledging results; buffering is configured externally. Output-only Universal Robots RTDE v2 telemetry is also available. Read-only ABB RWS1/RWS2 controller, mode, system, RAPID execution and named symbol values/properties are available with explicit API and environment credentials; RWS2 requires verified TLS. Exact text and separate host observation windows are retained. Epson Remote Ethernet monitoring uses explicit RC+7.5, RC+8 or RC800 profiles, external monitor-only setup, environment Login and qualified GETs for status, I/O, non-String variables, current robot and alarms where documented. Published 10/11 status widths stay raw; only the documented 11-flag form receives named flags. No Logout, control or motion commands are sent. Yaskawa HSES reads native status, current base position and explicit B/I/D/raw-R/whole-S32 variables with profile yrc1000_hw1483358_rev12 and an operator-declared UDP reply horizon; ephemeral port rotation or fixed-bind quarantine is limited to the source epoch. R encoding and disputed/unknown semantics remain raw; no motion or setup commands are sent. Native MTConnect probe/current/sample XML document capture binds exact observations, conditions and structured deltas to the reported model and agent epoch; it follows header cursors, reports caught-up checkpoints and fails on overwritten history or model/reset changes without silent rebasing. Published XML namespaces 1.2–1.8 and 2.0–2.7 are admitted; timestamps/units remain native. Passive Livox UDP sampling supports explicit SDK2 Mid360/S/L and HAP TX/T1 or legacy Horizon/Avia profiles with required points/imu selection, native coordinates/returns/IEEE words/raw clocks, mandatory SDK2 timestamp-and-payload CRC and immutable local raw groups. An external owner enables sampling and maintains any required heartbeat; peer/model declarations are unverified and do not imply scans or clock synchronization. Joint still/video/sensor runs use host monotonic frame-receive times; indexed videos map presentation frames to that timeline and can share one camera with still captures. Camera/video sources optionally configure one exact action_device_key on that shared worker before acquisition; owner loss fails without reconnecting or replaying the key. Custom Unix helper sources accept vendor SDK or protocol bridges. Hardware clock synchronization is not configured by Capturefab. See [industrial data](guides/industrial-data.md).

NI-DAQmx analog input: ni-daqmx feature (included by default), installed vendor runtime and supported Linux/Windows host. The isolated worker creates one fresh AI task with 1–64 individual physical channels. Omitted timing retains continuous internal-clock blocks. Explicit timing:on_demand requires integer poll_interval_ms from 1 to 3600000 and omits rate_hz/max_samples_per_channel/host_buffer_samples_per_channel, even null. Software mode leaves task timing unmodified, requests one scan per read and uses host pre-call admission spacing without catchup bursts or freshness/real-time promises. On-demand rows omit hardware-rate/buffer metadata and use original host completion clocks; ADC/auto-zero remain unchanged. Voltage configs remain the default; explicit thermocouple input declares per-channel type/units/ranges/built-in or constant CJC. Explicit current input declares per-channel terminal/ampere range/built-in or external shunt, with positive finite external ohms. Explicit RTD input requires per-channel type/temperature unit/range/wiring/R0 at zero Celsius and internal/external excitation amperes. Internal excitation can energize the sensor; external is an operator-supplied source. RTD settings stay request-only, with no inferred defaults or resistance/unit conversion and no universal NI-9216/9217 mode or hardware qualification. Explicit measurement:mixed combines required per-channel measurement tags, including same-family range/terminal differences, in one task without changing old configs or rows. Mixed blocks bind zero-based channel_index, actual physical, measurement, quantity, units and family requests in one channel_measurements array; raw words and finite family values retain their column units without global units or repeated sample tags. The selected constructor union and only needed TC setters resolve before task creation. Repeats remain; shared scans do not establish simultaneous or fresh conversions or per-channel timestamps. Software-only digital_port preserves whole-port unsigned U32 states with requested physical ports distinct from assigned read names and observed line counts; no pin labels or masks. counter_count/counter_frequency use one counter, explicit request fields and optional non-null input_terminal. Counter counts remain raw snapshots without unwrapping or hardware-width inference; frequency retains exact F64/finite Hz without host/count conversion. Both require on-demand timing, selected fixed input APIs and request-only source/method metadata. Input resource configuration is not passive; paired-counter methods and actual route/device support remain driver-specific. Exact F64 words and native status survive; finite temperature/amperes are never labeled volts or locally unit/V-R converted. Configured metadata is not hardware readback; built-in resistance and default terminals remain unqueried. Nominal rate and scan indices do not imply per-sample timestamps or synchronization. Partial native reads precede the original error; no reset, takeover, automatic restart or physical qualification claim. New AI measurements strain, bridge_ratio and acceleration also work in MixedAI with their own channel fields and units. Strain exposes seven bridge layouts and explicit gage/offset/ohms/Poisson requests; ratio supports volts_per_volt or millivolts_per_volt, and acceleration supports g/m_s2/in_s2 with separate sensitivity units. All three require explicit internal/external/none excitation amounts (volts or amperes); none is not a physical-disable guarantee. Optional ac/dc/ground coupling is request-only; ground measures ground, not sensor zero. Preserve raw IEEE plus finite strain/ratio/acceleration without local scaling. counter_period, counter_pulse_width, counter_angular_position and counter_linear_position are single-counter/on_demand-only F64 profiles with explicit time/edge/method or encoder PPR/distance/initial/Z requests. All Z fields are required even disabled; enabled Z can reset the measurement, and TwoPulse ignores phase. Omitted routes are unqueried and Z routes are rejected when disabled. Native time/position is never recomputed from host clocks or counts. Excitation may coerce/persist after Stop/Clear; no physical device, routing, power-off or OS/driver qualification is implied. See [NI input configuration](guides/industrial-data.md#ni-daqmx-analog-voltage-acquisition).

Additional `resistance`, `thermistor_current`, `thermistor_voltage`, `force_bridge`, `pressure_bridge` and `torque_bridge` profiles use1–64 typed AI channels, either timing mode and MixedAI18. Resistance returns ohms with explicit wiring/excitation. Thermistors require finite A/B/C for NI's Kelvin/ln(R) model without a guessed curve/sign rule; only voltage excitation needs positive reference `r1_ohms`, not RTD R0. Physical bridges keep output range/units separate from electrical and physical calibration units and preserve declared coordinate pairs. Equal electrical coordinates are rejected; descending/equal-physical requests retain any original native error. Per-channel `calibration_provenance:declared_two_point_linear_request` labels declared mapping, not measured/performed calibration. Native F64 and finite ohms/temperature/force/pressure/torque undergo no host equation, interpolation or unit math. Explicit excitation and optional ac/dc/ground coupling are request-only; none/Stop-Clear do not guarantee physical-off or native acceptance. All old rows remain unchanged, without sensor/module/driver/OS qualification. See [NI input configuration](guides/industrial-data.md#ni-daqmx-analog-voltage-acquisition).

Additional `velocity_iepe`, `force_iepe`, `charge_acceleration`, `lvdt` and `rvdt` measurements support both AI timing modes and MixedAI, now with eighteen channel kinds. Output units and sensitivity units are separate explicit requests: velocity m/s can use mV/(mm/s), charge acceleration uses pC sensitivity, LVDT includes mV/V per milli-inch, and RVDT uses angular sensitivity. The first three require terminal configuration; LVDT/RVDT instead require explicit AC excitation frequency and four/five/six-wire mode. All five preserve driver F64 words and finite velocity/force/acceleration/position/angle without local conversion. Sensitivity accepts finite signed and zero requests with native rejection preserved; older acceleration keeps its positive-only rule. Excitation and optional coupling remain requests, with no inferred calibration, delivered power or physical device qualification.

Installed GenTL/CTI drivers: configure CAPTUREFAB_GENTL_PRODUCERS or GENICAM_GENTL64_PATH, then use `list --kind gentl` and its complete ID. The default gentl feature runs drivers in an isolated helper; see [camera requirements](guides/camera-compatibility.md) for IMAGE/multipart still payload and XML limits. Ambiguous multipart errors supply copyable image_selectors camera IDs; local stills retain all components with bounded per-image multipart references in results. Companion JSON lists selectors for `Coord3D_C10p`, `Coord3D_C12p`, `Coord3D_C16` and `Confidence16` maps that can be saved as RAW or 16-bit PNG, and `Coord3D_ABC32f` point clouds that can be saved as RAW. Native GigE multipart local stills retain synchronized components in the documented unchunked stream layout. A default still requires one supported intensity image. Use `capture --part-format` with `Coord3D_C16`, `Confidence8`, `Confidence16`, `Mono16`, `Coord3D_C10p` or `Coord3D_C12p` for explicit local RAW or PNG selection, including streams without intensity. Use `Coord3D_ABC32f` to save a unique interleaved XYZ part as local RAW. Per-job `--part-format` also supports `Mono8`, `RGB8` and `YCbCr411_8` ordinary images; add `--part-index 0..31` to select an exact table ordinal with the expected type/PFNC checked on every frame. Equal-format reordering follows the ordinal, not a semantic identity. Same-camera jobs share one acquired frame and owner through the base selector; an explicitly bound GenTL URI keeps its binding. The industrial camera source uses the same formats through `part_format` and optional `part_index`. GenTL 1.6 stills can archive a supported complete GenDC container. Ordinary native GigE `Coord3D_ABC32f` profiles save as RAW with an interleaved float32 layout sidecar. Native GigE/USB and GenTL chunk artifacts retain raw bytes plus XML-derived values and units. Saved-file metadata and frame indexes preserve raw device timestamp ticks and optional frequency without assuming UTC.

LMI GoPxL: gopxl_ascii with profile gopxl_1_3_measurement, numeric Ethernet ASCII endpoint (async output disabled externally), declared delimiter, terminator crlf/cr/lf, invalid_token, trailing_delimiter absent/present/either and 1-64 named measurement IDs. Sends only measurement,<ids>; keeps raw text, scaled_i32, exact three-decimal value and pass/decision_invalid bits; ERROR/malformed/extra bytes withhold the poll, no retry/reconnect. Binary GoPxL GDP unsupported. See https://capturefab.com/guides/industrial-data.md#lmi-gopxl-measurements-over-ethernet-ascii
Opto 22 groov EPIC/RIO: optommp with profile groov_expanded_inputs, model epic_pr1/epic_pr2/rio_mm1/rio_mm2, numeric TCP endpoint and 1-64 channels {name,module,channel,resource analog_eu|digital_state,expected_module_id,expected_channel_type} checked against the documented input allowlist. Powerup Clear must be cleared externally; every poll rechecks unit type/PUC/module/type and reads value plus native quality with ReadQuadlet only under one deadline; failed polls are withheld whole. Exact binary32/U32 words, native quality codes, units externally_configured_unqueried; no writes, read-clear, retry or reconnect. See https://capturefab.com/guides/industrial-data.md#opto-22-groov-inputs-over-optommp
Atlas Copco PF6000: atlas_open_protocol with explicit pf6000_v2_8 profile and numeric Virtual Station endpoint; provision Disconnect=None externally. Startup5/result3, native scaled integers/codes/local time/raw frames, JSONL checkpoint before ACK within original read deadline; OS-reported sync is not a universal power-loss guarantee or exactly-once proof. No reconnect/history/tool commands. See https://capturefab.com/guides/industrial-data.md#atlas-copco-pf6000-tightening-results
